newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Witnesses identify Serb in Swiss war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses identify Serb in Swiss war crimes trial.

text.p: Witnesses on Tuesday identified a Bosnian Serb accused of torture and murder during the Yugoslav war in Switzerland's first ever war crimes trial, Swiss news agency ATS said.

Goran Grabez, a 32-year-old former driver from the Bosnian town of Prijedor, faces a maximum 20 years jail if found guilty on four counts of war crimes committed at the Serb-run Omarska detention camp in northwestern Bosnia in July 1992.
ATS said Grabez pleaded not guilty on Tuesday, the second day of his week-long military trial in the city of Lausanne.
But two unidentified prosecution witnesses recognised Grabez as one of the Bosnian Serb guards at Omarska, ATS said.
One of them, a Bosnian Moslem survivor from Omarska, told the court that he saw Grabez, carrying a truncheon, enter a house where Bosnian Serbs used to torture their victims.
Grabez, arrested two years ago in Geneva after Moslem refugees alleged he was a guard at Omarska and had tortured inmates, denies the allegations and says he was in Austria and Germany at the time.
